curriculum: The exact Dutch-plus-English 180 EC Pharmacy bachelor target uses the Farmacie study path rather than Farmaceutische Wetenschappen or the English-taught College of Pharmaceutical Sciences. Appendix B and the student site establish 135 EC required major and 45 EC of profiling with the 7.5 EC thesis. The alternative 15 EC thesis replaces it and gives 142.5 EC major and 37.5 EC profiling. All three Academic Skills courses carry no credits and are compulsory. The first-year Academic Skills pass releases the credits for Drug Research. The standard example contains 52.5 EC of credited level 1 requirements, 37.5 EC of level 2 and 45 EC of level 3, including the thesis. The Dutch current course catalogue and EER show Cardiovascular Disorders, Chronic Inflammatory Disorders and Dermatological Preparations and Skin Disorders as the updated titles.
progression: The first displayed enrolment pattern has Year 2 P1 Infection and Immunity plus Hormonal Disorders, P2 Biologics and one elective, P3 Product Care and one elective, P4 Neurology and one elective. Year 3 P1 Chronic Inflammatory Disorders and the 7.5 EC thesis use different slots (BC and AD), P2 Cardiovascular Disorders and Oncology, P3 Psychopharmacology and one elective, P4 Skin Disorders and one elective. This closes 60 EC each year and meets the three follow-course sequences. Required level 3 courses require passes in all compulsory level 1 courses. In addition, FA-BA203, FA-BA201 and FA-BA202 must be followed before FA-BA301, FA-BA303 and FA-BA305 respectively. The thesis catalogue requires enrolment in Farmacie, all first-year courses and skills, and describes previous writing practice, Neurology and an approved topic with supervisor and examiner. The 7.5 EC thesis requires approximately 200 hours over 10 weeks and has a single final result. The standard profile requires at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3, no double-counting overlapping content and prior approval for study outside Utrecht. The ordinary first-year study advice threshold is 45 EC.
